sentences.text:
Kamlesh Kahar vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12
November, 2024
 Neutral Citation No. 2024:Mphc-Jbp:55763
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 12 th Of November, 2024
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 43283 of 2024
 Kamlesh Kahar
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh
 Appearance:
 Shri Pradeep K. Sharma - Advocate for applicant.
 Shri C.M. Tiwari - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS Act for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 698/2024 registered at Police Station - Gadarwara, District- Narsinghpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 of IPC.
Applicant is in detention since 30.06.2024.
Previous bail application was dismissed on merits.

2. As per the prosecution story, allegation against the applicant is that he alongwith co-accused,
cheated Rs.78 lakh 71 thousand from the complainant and other people.
After investigation, offence under the aforesaid section has been registered against the applicant and co-accused.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is in jail since 30.06.2024.
It is submitted that present applicant is not the main accused.
Main accused is Yashwant Prajapati.
He has been made accused only on the basis of memorandum.
Even he has been cheated by the co-accused persons and in this regard wife of the present applicant has submitted an application before the Superintendent of Police on 24.06.2024.
He has not received any amount.
Co- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:55763 2 MCRC-43283-2024 accused Pramila Prajapati has granted by the trial Court on 24.10.2024 and charge sheet has been filed on 26.09.2024.
Applicant has no criminal past and conclusion of the trial will take considerable time

,
therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant.

sentences.text: Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, but without commenting on merit of the case, I am inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Consequently, bail application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant, stands allowed.

6. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for his regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that he shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.
He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS.
7. This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
8. Certified copy as per rules.
